in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes - I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does he live with you, and are you responsible for his day-to-day care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he doesn't actually live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mum, I need to understand the situation a bit more.

Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep at least at the same level as the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for a first or only child)? This could be through maintenance payments or other regular financial support.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. 

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex's mum is the one who is primarily responsible for him day-to-day since he lives with her. 

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you generally need to be responsible for the child, which usually means either:
- The child lives with you, **or**
- You contribute towards the cost of looking after them at least at the same rate as the Child Benefit amount

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently contributing financially towards his care, I'm afraid you wouldn't be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. His mum, as the person he lives with and who is responsible for his day-to-day care, would likely be the eligible person to make a claim.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment:

Since Alex lives with his mum and you're not currently contributing financially towards his care, you don't meet the responsibility requirement.

**What this means:**
Alex's mum would likely be the eligible person to claim Child Benefit for him, as she is responsible for his day-to-day care.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you begin contributing financially at the required level—you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time.
